passage: Why do dolphins leap out of the water but whales typically remain submerged? Scientists theorize that this difference in behavior between the two marine mammal species may be related to their body size and energy efficiency. Dolphins, being much smaller and more agile than whales, can launch themselves into the air with relatively little energy expenditure, and this behavior may help them navigate, communicate, or remove parasites. Whales, however, require enormous amounts of energy to propel their massive bodies out of the water, making such behavior energetically costly. For whales, remaining submerged and using other communication methods may be far more efficient than breaching.
